articles.title: Understand registries and registers
articles.purpose: A registry is the application for a domain; a register is a structured dataset inside it.
articles.steps:
Identify the correct registry service.
Choose the register that stores the required entity.
Check related records and linked identifiers before entering data.
articles.requirements: Existing registry access.
articles.next_step: Open the relevant intake or record screen.
articles.issues: Different registers have different fields; do not treat a household and a person as the same record.

articles.title: Understand proposed and approved record changes
articles.purpose: A proposed change is separate from the approved record until its workflow completes.
articles.steps:
Open the record and identify the section to change.
Describe the proposed correction and attach required evidence.
Submit through the configured review process.
Check the request status before assuming the live record changed.
articles.requirements: Record editing permission and evidence.
articles.next_step: Track verification and approval.
articles.issues: A saved proposal does not by itself prove that the approved record has changed.

sources.title: KarnatakaDBT documentation: change management and approval workflow

articles.title: Read the record workflow audit
articles.purpose: Workflow evidence and actor timestamps explain who initiated, checked and approved a change.
articles.steps:
Locate the change request for the record.
Review the submitted evidence and recorded actors.
Compare the decision and time with the reported issue.
articles.requirements: Permission to view the request and audit information.
articles.next_step: Escalate discrepancies with the request reference.
articles.issues: A workflow trail differs from a snapshot of the record at a particular time.

sources.title: KarnatakaDBT documentation: audit ability and trace ability

articles.title: Attach and review record documents
articles.purpose: Record file fields and evidence attached to a change request serve different purposes.
articles.steps:
Check the file field label, allowed type and maximum size.
Upload the required file into its intended slot.
Confirm it appears before saving or submitting.
Use the view control to inspect the file when reviewing evidence.
articles.requirements: Document access and the required file.
articles.next_step: Submit the proposed record or change for review.
articles.issues: Supporting evidence on a change request may not become a permanent record file after approval.

articles.title: Monitor imported registry submissions
articles.purpose: Partner and staff ingestion can create intake submissions or proposed updates.
articles.steps:
Identify the source, target register and intake form.
Retain the returned correlation reference.
Check classification, transformation and processing status where available.
Investigate failed items before resubmitting.
articles.requirements: An authorised integration and supported ingestion configuration.
articles.next_step: Verify the resulting submission or change request.
articles.issues: Acceptance by an API is not proof of successful registry processing; do not repeatedly send the same payload.

articles.title: Inspect committed record history
articles.purpose: Record history shows approved snapshots and associated changes.
articles.steps:
Open Version History if it is available on the record.
Choose the relevant date.
Compare the changed sections and linked request.
articles.requirements: History viewing permission.
articles.next_step: Use the evidence for an authorised correction or investigation.
articles.issues: History, workflow audit and computed-score history are different views; availability depends on the installed release.

articles.title: Follow the registry intake lifecycle
articles.purpose: Intake progresses from a saved form through submission, review and backend processing.
articles.steps:
Choose the target register and intake form.
Complete required fields and save a draft.
Submit and retain the application reference.
Track review and processing separately.
articles.requirements: Configured intake form and intake access.
articles.next_step: Verify that processing completed and the record exists.
articles.issues: Submitted forms may be locked. Approval and successful backend processing are separate milestones.

articles.title: Understand consent-aware registry sharing
articles.purpose: Documented sharing separates the consent decision from enforcement by the registry.
articles.steps:
Identify the recipient, purpose and requested data.
Check the applicable consent and partner policy.
Use the authorised integration to request only the effective permitted fields.
articles.requirements: Configured consent enforcement and an authorised recipient.
articles.next_step: Record the decision reference or resolve a denial.
articles.issues: Documentation does not prove that every connector in this sandbox enforces the same consent flow.

sources.title: KarnatakaDBT documentation: consent aware data sharing

articles.title: Review potential duplicate registry records
articles.purpose: Deduplication produces candidates according to configured fields and matching rules.
articles.steps:
Check whether deduplication is enabled for the register.
Review the flagged candidates and supporting identity data.
Escalate uncertain matches through the authorised workflow.
articles.requirements: Duplicate-review access and configured matching rules.
articles.next_step: Record the reviewed outcome through available controls.
articles.issues: A similarity score is a review signal, not proof that two people are the same. Administrators control thresholds.

articles.title: Understand role-based access
articles.purpose: Operational and configuration permissions are assigned through the identity system.
articles.steps:
Identify the task and its required permission.
Check the assigned application and account role.
Ask the access administrator to resolve a missing permission.
articles.requirements: Existing identity and access administration process.
articles.next_step: Sign in again after an approved role change.
articles.issues: Default upstream role names may differ from KarnatakaDBT roles. Choosing a persona does not grant access.

sources.title: KarnatakaDBT documentation: rbac roles and permissions

articles.title: Understand registry export jobs
articles.purpose: Documented export jobs can include a chosen register and related records.
articles.steps:
Confirm the filtered or selected scope.
Choose an available export format.
Monitor the job in export history.
Check the downloaded file and related-record coverage.
articles.requirements: Export permission; the export feature must exist in the installed release.
articles.next_step: Handle the output using the approved reporting process.
articles.issues: A retry may use current filters rather than the previous row selection. Check scope before retrying.

articles.title: Distinguish programme processing rules
articles.purpose: Eligibility, disbursement selection and entitlement are separate rule decisions.
articles.steps:
Identify which decision is being configured.
Use the programme-approved criteria for that decision.
Test with fictional examples and inspect the resulting status.
articles.requirements: Programme management permission and approved rule definitions.
articles.next_step: Send the result through configured verification.
articles.issues: Do not infer benefit amounts from eligibility alone; missing or stale registry data can affect results.

articles.title: Distinguish enrolment and disbursement cycles
articles.purpose: Enrolment cycles select beneficiaries; disbursement cycles organise delivery of benefits.
articles.steps:
Select the programme and identify the cycle type.
Check its dates and source beneficiary list.
Apply the configured rules and review the resulting list.
articles.requirements: Programme access and configured cycles.
articles.next_step: Follow the relevant list verification process.
articles.issues: Newer PBMS documentation describes dual cycles; verify the controls present in this installation.

articles.title: Review programme lists before finalisation
articles.purpose: Configured verifications provide evidence and accountability before a list is finalised.
articles.steps:
Open the relevant enrolment or disbursement list.
Check the required verification stage.
Review the supporting information and record your authorised assessment.
articles.requirements: Assigned verification permission.
articles.next_step: Send the list to the next configured reviewer.
articles.issues: Do not claim a list is verified simply because it has been generated.

articles.title: Correct the source of beneficiary lists
articles.purpose: Documented PBMS list generation uses registry data as its source.
articles.steps:
Identify the incorrect source record.
Correct it through the registry workflow.
Confirm the approved change before generating a replacement list where permitted.
articles.requirements: Registry correction and programme permissions.
articles.next_step: Review the regenerated list and its cycle state.
articles.issues: Approved cycles may prevent new lists. Do not edit exported lists to simulate a registry correction.

articles.title: Understand bank reconciliation
articles.purpose: Reconciliation compares disbursement references with bank transaction evidence.
articles.steps:
Check the programme, cycle and disbursement reference.
Review the returned transaction or statement evidence in the configured reconciliation service.
Escalate unmatched or inconsistent items.
articles.requirements: A configured reconciliation integration and assigned staff permission.
articles.next_step: Record the resolved reconciliation result.
articles.issues: The upstream guide describes sponsor-bank statements and Bridge processing. This sandbox does not issue real payments.

sources.title: KarnatakaDBT documentation: reconciliation with sponsor bank

articles.title: Use programme reports and dashboards
articles.purpose: Programme reporting can cover beneficiary statistics, transactions and reconciliation.
articles.steps:
Open the relevant dashboard.
Confirm its dataset, period and programme filters.
Check whether its numbers represent people, households, applications or transactions.
articles.requirements: Dashboard viewing permission and a configured dataset.
articles.next_step: Use the filtered results in authorised reporting.
articles.issues: A dashboard may not refresh immediately when source records change; check its update time.

articles.title: Understand programme fund records
articles.purpose: A programme fund records an allocation against the chosen programme and company.
articles.steps:
Open programme accounting if available.
Check the programme, company, date and amount on the fund record.
Follow the finance team’s authorised process for any proposed allocation.
articles.requirements: Finance authority and the relevant accounting feature.
articles.next_step: Review the allocation using the programme finance workflow.
articles.issues: Examples in upstream documentation do not define KarnatakaDBT budgets or authorise a transfer. Use fictional amounts in the sandbox.

articles.title: Review cycle manager settings
articles.purpose: A cycle manager defines the configured behaviour of programme benefit cycles.
articles.steps:
Open the programme configuration.
Inspect its cycle manager and available settings.
Confirm the intended cycle behaviour with the programme owner before changing it.
articles.requirements: Programme configuration authority.
articles.next_step: Test the configuration using a demonstration cycle.
articles.issues: Older cycle-manager screens differ from newer PBMS. Do not enable automatic approval without an approved policy.

sources.title: KarnatakaDBT documentation: create cycle manager for a program

articles.title: Create an individual registrant in the legacy registry
articles.purpose: Legacy registry screens collect a person’s identifying and personal details.
articles.steps:
Open Registry and choose Individual.
Use Create if your account has the required permission.
Enter the mandatory names and the configured personal details.
Review and save the record.
articles.requirements: Registrar access and the information required by the form.
articles.next_step: Link the person to the correct household or programme as required.
articles.issues: This guide applies to the legacy registry; modern intake uses a different review workflow. Use fictional identities here.

sources.title: KarnatakaDBT documentation: create an individual registrant

articles.title: Link members to a household or group
articles.purpose: Legacy groups can link existing individual registrants as members.
articles.steps:
Open the group or household.
Use the Members section to select existing individuals.
Check each person and membership relationship.
Review and save the proposed membership.
articles.requirements: Group-editing permission and the member records.
articles.next_step: Check the saved membership and any applicable review status.
articles.issues: A person’s name alone is insufficient to identify the correct record; compare the authorised identifiers.

sources.title: KarnatakaDBT documentation: create a group and add individual registrants to the group

articles.title: Maintain configured identifier types
articles.purpose: Identifier types define the options used when storing registrant IDs.
articles.steps:
Open registry configuration if authorised.
Inspect existing ID Types before proposing a new one.
Use the approved identifier name and save through the available process.
articles.requirements: Registry configuration authority.
articles.next_step: Use the configured type when entering an identifier.
articles.issues: An identifier type is a label and does not by itself verify a Synthetic identity ID or other identity.

articles.title: Maintain relationship definitions
articles.purpose: Relationships can define source and destination entity types and an inverse label.
articles.steps:
Review existing relationship definitions.
Confirm the intended direction and entity types.
Enter the approved name and inverse name where the form requires them.
articles.requirements: Registry configuration authority.
articles.next_step: Test the relationship on fictional records.
articles.issues: Membership and relationship definitions must match the intended household model; do not create duplicate labels.

articles.title: Validate a CSV import before loading
articles.purpose: Legacy import maps spreadsheet columns to registry fields.
articles.steps:
Choose the correct register and Import records if available.
Upload a fictional test file.
Map each column to its intended field.
Run Test and resolve errors before Import.
articles.requirements: Import permission and a correctly formatted file.
articles.next_step: Check imported records, IDs and relationships.
articles.issues: A successful file upload does not validate mappings. Retain identifiers to avoid accidental duplicate imports.

sources.title: KarnatakaDBT documentation: import csv file to registry module

articles.title: Understand proxy means test configuration
articles.purpose: A PMT combines configured household indicators and weights for programme assessment.
articles.steps:
Open the programme’s PMT configuration where available.
Compare fields and weights with the approved scoring specification.
Test expected outcomes with fictional household examples.
articles.requirements: Programme configuration authority and approved scoring rules.
articles.next_step: Review the results before applying the programme process.
articles.issues: The library supplies no Karnatakan eligibility threshold. AI must not invent weights, cutoffs or policy rules.

sources.title: KarnatakaDBT documentation: configure proxy means test

articles.title: Understand eligibility reassessment
articles.purpose: Older PBMS supports reassessing enrolled registrants against updated configured criteria.
articles.steps:
Confirm the programme and reason for reassessment.
Review the approved criteria and current enrolled list.
Use Verify eligibility only through the authorised programme process.
Check resulting beneficiary statuses.
articles.requirements: Programme management authority and existing enrolled records.
articles.next_step: Review any changed status and communicate through the approved process.
articles.issues: Reassessment can affect beneficiary status; do not run it casually or treat a draft registrant as enrolled.

sources.title: KarnatakaDBT documentation: verify eligibility of enrolled registrants

articles.title: Check programme duplicate status
articles.purpose: Programme deduplication uses the programme’s configured deduplication manager.
articles.steps:
Open the programme and inspect its beneficiaries.
Review the configured duplicate-check rules.
Run the available check only when authorised and inspect flagged statuses.
articles.requirements: Programme administration permission.
articles.next_step: Investigate candidate duplicates before the next programme step.
articles.issues: A Duplicated status requires review; do not delete or merge records solely on a matching name.

articles.title: Interpret programme enrolment results
articles.purpose: Configured programme criteria determine which draft candidates become enrolled.
articles.steps:
Open the programme and inspect candidate statuses.
Confirm the applicable eligibility configuration.
Use the authorised enrolment workflow.
Review Enrolled and Not Eligible results.
articles.requirements: Programme management permission and candidate records.
articles.next_step: Continue to the configured verification or benefit cycle.
articles.issues: Registration, eligibility and enrolment are distinct states; an application is not a payment confirmation.

sources.title: KarnatakaDBT documentation: enrol registrants into program

articles.title: Understand staged entitlement assessment
articles.purpose: Older PBMS can assign entitlement assessment to multiple managers in sequence.
articles.steps:
Check the programme’s assessment stage and your assignment.
Review evidence and record the assessment required at your stage.
Submit through the configured entitlement workflow.
articles.requirements: Configured staged assessment and the appropriate manager role.
articles.next_step: Allow the next authorised stage to review the assessment.
articles.issues: Only assigned stages can carry out their actions. An assessment recommendation is not an approved payment.

articles.title: Review programme notification configuration
articles.purpose: A notification manager connects programme events to configured notification behaviour.
articles.steps:
Open the programme configuration.
Inspect the assigned notification manager and provider type.
Confirm permitted templates and recipient behaviour using fictional test data.
articles.requirements: Programme configuration permission and an enabled provider.
articles.next_step: Check the test notification outcome.
articles.issues: A configured manager does not prove delivery. Avoid sending live messages during a client demonstration.

articles.title: Map field collection data into the registry
articles.purpose: An ODK importer transforms selected submission fields into individual or group records.
articles.steps:
Identify the ODK form and target registry.
Check that the form has its intended importer and field mapping.
Test a fictional submission and inspect the transformed values.
articles.requirements: ODK/import administration access and a supported mapping configuration.
articles.next_step: Validate the imported record and its processing status.
articles.issues: Mappings are form-specific. An ODK submission is not automatically a verified beneficiary.

sources.title: KarnatakaDBT documentation: customize the odk importer configuration based on the odk form fields

articles.title: Understand importing a registry data source into PBMS
articles.purpose: Legacy PBMS can use configured data sources to retrieve social registry records.
articles.steps:
Check the source service and the target individual or group register.
Have the authorised administrator confirm endpoint and authentication configuration.
Test a small fictional dataset and check field mapping.
articles.requirements: Approved integration access and a configured data source.
articles.next_step: Verify imported records before programme processing.
articles.issues: Do not place passwords or tokens in knowledge content. Source and target identifiers must remain consistent.

sources.title: KarnatakaDBT documentation: import social registry data into pbms

articles.title: Understand application and login-provider administration
articles.purpose: The IAM admin console describes registered applications and their login providers.
articles.steps:
Open Applications to inspect the service’s registered URL and identifier.
Review the associated Login Providers.
Escalate an incorrect mapping to the authorised access administrator.
articles.requirements: IAM administration access.
articles.next_step: Test the existing sign-in route after an approved correction.
articles.issues: Application registration and persona selection are separate from operational permission assignment.

articles.title: Understand shared reference code lists
articles.purpose: Code lists provide stable codes and labels for values used across services.
articles.steps:
Choose the relevant reference dataset.
Check the code, label and parent value where applicable.
Confirm the version or effective date if the installed service provides them.
articles.requirements: Master-data viewing access.
articles.next_step: Use the approved code rather than inventing a free-text value.
articles.issues: Newer catalogue versioning is documented upstream; this installation may expose the earlier attribute/value interface.

articles.title: Plan administrative geography changes
articles.purpose: Upstream catalogue guidance treats hierarchy and boundaries as a consistent geography version.
articles.steps:
Identify the official change and its effective date.
Check affected parent and child units.
Prepare an old-to-new code mapping for reports and consumers.
Use the authorised reference-data change process.
articles.requirements: Approved geographic reference information and administration authority.
articles.next_step: Validate consuming forms and maps after the change.
articles.issues: Do not overwrite a household’s recorded Taluk merely because its state or a boundary label changes.

articles.title: Review changes to shared reference data
articles.purpose: Newer catalogue guidance uses drafts and approvals before publishing versioned changes.
articles.steps:
Identify the proposed change and its owner.
Review the affected values and consumers.
Submit through the change controls available in the installed release.
articles.requirements: Reference-data change authority.
articles.next_step: Confirm the published values and their effective date.
articles.issues: Do not assume draft/publish controls exist in older interfaces; ask the administrator to confirm the supported process.

articles.title: Navigate the reference-data administration interface
articles.purpose: The current upstream catalogue UI groups datasets, geography, releases and activity.
articles.steps:
Identify the installed interface and its menu labels.
Locate the dataset or geography entry you need.
Inspect codes, labels and available history before proposing changes.
articles.requirements: Master-data access.
articles.next_step: Use the authorised edit or review process for the selected item.
articles.issues: The local version may use Attributes and Values rather than the newer catalogue pages.

articles.title: Understand approval stages and quorum
articles.purpose: Approval policies can combine sequential stages, parallel groups and required approval counts.
articles.steps:
Identify the request’s active policy.
Check the current stage and assigned approvers.
Determine whether all, a configured count or a percentage must approve.
articles.requirements: Request-view permission and a configured policy.
articles.next_step: Complete your assigned task and monitor the next stage.
articles.issues: Your individual approval may not complete the stage; newer policy options may not exist in this release.

articles.title: Understand approval policy versions
articles.purpose: A policy defines stages and rules; requests can remain tied to the version they started with.
articles.steps:
Inspect the policy version attached to the request.
Compare its stage rules with the active configuration.
Prepare changes in a new draft where that versioning interface is available.
articles.requirements: Approval administration authority for configuration changes.
articles.next_step: Test the revised policy before activation.
articles.issues: Changing a policy does not necessarily change requests already in progress.

articles.title: Understand overdue task escalation
articles.purpose: An SLA policy determines what happens when an assigned task passes its due time.
articles.steps:
Check the due time and current stage.
Inspect the configured breach action.
Contact the responsible supervisor through the approved escalation process.
articles.requirements: Task-view access; administrative authority to change policies.
articles.next_step: Track the actual escalation result in request history.
articles.issues: An overdue task is not automatically approved. Upstream permits several actions; confirm this deployment’s configured behaviour.

articles.title: Understand separation of approval duties
articles.purpose: Policy settings can prevent requesters or earlier-stage approvers from approving later work.
articles.steps:
Check your relationship to the request.
Review the available assigned task.
Use the independent reviewer route required by the policy.
articles.requirements: Assigned approver permission.
articles.next_step: Escalate a stage with no eligible approver.
articles.issues: A role alone may not make you eligible for every task; do not bypass separation rules by changing accounts.

articles.title: Understand reassignment of a blocked approval task
articles.purpose: The documented admin workflow closes the old task and creates one for a new assignee.
articles.steps:
Open the request and locate the unresolved task.
Confirm why reassignment is needed and who is authorised to receive it.
Have an authorised administrator use Reassign if available.
Check the resulting task and audit entry.
articles.requirements: Approval administrator permission.
articles.next_step: The new assignee reviews the task.
articles.issues: Reassignment is not approval. The original due time may remain in effect.

articles.title: Understand partner onboarding and public keys
articles.purpose: Partner management stores partner identity, lifecycle and signing public keys.
articles.steps:
Check the stable partner identifier and organisation.
Inspect the onboarding request and proposed public keys.
Use the authorised review process to activate or reject the request.
articles.requirements: Partner administration and review permission.
articles.next_step: Verify the partner and key status for the intended integration.
articles.issues: A created partner or pending key is not automatically active. Never put private keys in guidance or uploaded public-key fields.

articles.title: Understand partner signature verification
articles.purpose: Integrations can retrieve active partner public keys from partner management.
articles.steps:
Confirm that the caller’s partner identifier matches the onboarded identifier.
Check partner activation and key validity.
Ask the integration administrator to inspect key retrieval and signature failures.
articles.requirements: An approved integration and its responsible administrator.
articles.next_step: Retest an authorised fictional request.
articles.issues: Disabled or unknown partners must not be treated as trusted merely because a prior key is cached.

articles.title: Understand effective consent scope
articles.purpose: Documented consent decisions restrict sharing to the intersection of requested, granted and policy-permitted data.
articles.steps:
Check the subject, recipient, purpose and requested fields.
Review the validation result and effective scopes.
Release data only through a configured enforcement integration.
articles.requirements: Consent-policy access and a supported integration.
articles.next_step: Retain the decision reference or resolve the denial.
articles.issues: A broad request does not authorise broad sharing; upstream design details may differ from the installed implementation.

articles.title: Understand consent policies for partners
articles.purpose: A consent policy limits what a partner can receive from a specified data controller.
articles.steps:
Identify the partner and controller.
Review the permitted purpose, scopes and validity constraints.
Send policy changes through the authorised approval process.
articles.requirements: Consent administration authority.
articles.next_step: Test the resulting decision using fictional subjects.
articles.issues: Newer documentation separates partner identity from consent bindings. Confirm this deployment’s version before applying those screens.

sources.title: KarnatakaDBT documentation: partner onboarding and policy

articles.title: Understand consent lifecycle and withdrawal
articles.purpose: Consent can progress through request, authentication, grant, expiry or revocation.
articles.steps:
Review who is requesting data and why.
Use the configured subject consent flow to grant or decline.
Check active status and expiry before use.
Use the authorised revocation route when withdrawing a grant.
articles.requirements: A configured consent flow and the appropriate subject or administrative authority.
articles.next_step: Check the receipt and updated status where supported.
articles.issues: A pending request is not an active grant. Consent collection and registry enforcement may use different integration paths.

articles.title: Prepare a dashboard import
articles.purpose: Superset can import packaged dashboard definitions linked to configured datasets.
articles.steps:
Have an authorised analytics administrator confirm the target data connection.
Choose a compatible dashboard ZIP package.
Import through the available dashboard controls.
Open the result and check every chart and filter.
articles.requirements: Dashboard import permission and an approved data connection.
articles.next_step: Validate counts against the source dataset.
articles.issues: Never paste database credentials into help text; imported charts may require connection or schema corrections.

sources.title: KarnatakaDBT documentation: importing dashboards on the superset ui for opeka2p applications

articles.title: Follow the KarnatakaDBT service journey
articles.purpose: Know which application handles each part of the demonstration.
articles.steps:
Start with the persona workspace or All services.
Register the household and submit it for independent review.
After approval, track the programme application, eligibility and enrolment through the relevant service.
Use reporting to inspect recorded outcomes.
articles.requirements: An existing account with the required task permissions.
articles.next_step: Open help at the stage you are working on.
articles.issues: Household approval does not itself grant a benefit or prove a payment. Demonstration records are fictional.

articles.title: Understand personas and account permissions
articles.purpose: Personas organise the experience around citizen, registration, verification and supervision tasks.
articles.steps:
Choose the persona relevant to the client walkthrough.
Read the task list and current status.
Sign in with an authorised account to perform available actions.
articles.requirements: Existing account permission for any operational action.
articles.next_step: Use the linked service for your assigned task.
articles.issues: The persona selector and demo walkthrough cannot grant new permissions.

articles.title: Prepare a household registration
articles.purpose: Collect the information required by the household form before submission.
articles.steps:
Check required household details and location fields.
Check member details and relationships.
Save and review the draft.
Resolve form errors, then submit once for review.
articles.requirements: Fictional household information for this sandbox.
articles.next_step: Retain the reference and track the submitted status.
articles.issues: Submission is different from approval. Avoid creating another household merely because review is pending.

articles.title: Respond to a returned registration
articles.purpose: Use reviewer feedback to correct the original household submission.
articles.steps:
Open the returned record.
Read the reason for correction.
Update the relevant fields and check the household members and location.
Resubmit through the form when the application allows it.
articles.requirements: Access to the returned household and its feedback.
articles.next_step: Track the new review status.
articles.issues: Correct the original record instead of making a duplicate application.

articles.title: Prepare an independent registration review
articles.purpose: A verifier checks the submitted information and recorded evidence before deciding.
articles.steps:
Open a pending record assigned or available to your account.
Compare household details, members and geographic information.
Read recorded evidence and provenance.
Use the available decision controls with a useful reason for any return.
articles.requirements: Verification permission and access to the submitted record.
articles.next_step: Check the resulting status and activity record.
articles.issues: A map dot or AI answer is not identity or residence verification.

articles.title: Investigate a registration status question
articles.purpose: Use the record reference and activity rather than relying on recollection.
articles.steps:
Find the household or submission reference.
Inspect the current review status and recorded activity.
Compare feedback and the relevant timestamp.
Escalate discrepancies to the responsible staff member.
articles.requirements: Permission to inspect the record.
articles.next_step: Follow the appropriate correction or review process.
articles.issues: Screens may show different stages of processing. Do not approve a case just to resolve a display inconsistency.

articles.title: Prepare a programme application
articles.purpose: A programme application is a separate step after the required registration process.
articles.steps:
Check that the household registration has the required status.
Open the programme application route available to your account.
Review the programme and required form information.
Submit and retain the application reference.
articles.requirements: An eligible application route and the information required by the programme.
articles.next_step: Track the application and its eligibility/enrolment status.
articles.issues: The library does not define government eligibility rules. Use only the programme criteria configured and approved by its owner.

articles.title: Interpret household and programme statuses
articles.purpose: Understand what the application has actually recorded at each stage.
articles.steps:
Read the household review status first.
Check the programme application separately.
Distinguish pending review, returned details, approved registration, eligibility and enrolment.
Use the current screen’s next-step guidance.
articles.requirements: Access to your household or assigned record.
articles.next_step: Ask the responsible officer about a blocked stage.
articles.issues: Approved registration and enrolled status are not confirmation of a real payment in this sandbox.

articles.title: Interpret state colours on the Karnataka map
articles.purpose: State shading summarises the records included by the current map filters.
articles.steps:
Check the selected filters and counting unit.
Read the colour legend before comparing states.
Inspect the displayed state count.
Use household points to examine coordinate coverage rather than infer approval or need.
articles.requirements: Geography page access.
articles.next_step: Compare the map with the filtered record list and coverage summary.
articles.issues: A darker state indicates more included records, not a higher poverty rate or a verified population estimate.

articles.title: Check household coordinate quality
articles.purpose: Coordinate provenance determines whether a household point is useful beyond a demonstration.
articles.steps:
Check latitude, longitude and coordinate source.
Distinguish synthetic demo points from captured or verified residence points.
Keep the recorded state and Taluk structure intact.
Flag missing or inconsistent locations for authorised correction.
articles.requirements: Permission to view geographic records.
articles.next_step: Review the coverage and coordinate provenance summary.
articles.issues: Demo points are not verified households or Taluk positions. Do not infer a new Taluk from a synthetic coordinate.

articles.title: Choose the correct staff service
articles.purpose: Use the staff portal and shared navigation to reach the task-specific application.
articles.steps:
Sign in through the existing staff route.
Choose the service for your task.
Confirm the application and record context before acting.
Open stage help when the next step is unclear.
articles.requirements: An existing staff account and assigned permissions.
articles.next_step: Continue the task in the target service.
articles.issues: Access to one service does not imply permission for every other service.

articles.title: Resolve a staff access problem
articles.purpose: Separate an expired session from a missing task permission.
articles.steps:
Confirm the correct service and staff sign-in route.
Sign in again if the session has expired.
Check whether the task is assigned and the required role is present.
Report the service, screen and error to the access administrator without sharing credentials.
articles.requirements: Your existing account and a non-sensitive problem description.
articles.next_step: Retry after the authorised correction.
articles.issues: Never put passwords, session cookies or tokens into knowledge articles or AI questions.

articles.title: Use source-linked task guidance
articles.purpose: Library articles explain local tasks or summarise official upstream reference material.
articles.steps:
Check the article’s service and workflow stage.
Read its local-workflow or upstream-reference label.
Use the source link for further detail.
Confirm release-dependent features with the application administrator.
articles.requirements: Published library access.
articles.next_step: Follow the actual controls available to your account.
articles.issues: An upstream feature description is not proof that the feature is enabled in KarnatakaDBT.

articles.title: Maintain a guidance article
articles.purpose: Staff can update guidance through the existing versioned review process.
articles.steps:
Open Manage guidance with an authorised account.
Create or edit the service, stage, audience and six guidance fields.
Save the draft and submit for independent review.
An authorised reviewer checks it before supervisor publication.
articles.requirements: Existing knowledge editing/review/publication permissions.
articles.next_step: Verify the published version in the library and screen help.
articles.issues: Drafts remain separate from published content. Authors cannot review their own drafts.

articles.title: Check a local AI answer
articles.purpose: The local assistant retrieves published guidance and presents relevant source links.
articles.steps:
Select the service, role and workflow stage.
Ask a task question without personal information.
Read the linked source articles and any version caveats.
Use the application’s authorised controls for the actual task.
articles.requirements: An existing account and an available local model.
articles.next_step: Consult an authorised staff member if guidance is insufficient.
articles.issues: AI may be wrong and cannot verify identities, approve cases, set policy or initiate payments.

articles.title: Review AI-suggested guidance before saving
articles.purpose: A generated suggestion is editable form text, not a published rule.
articles.steps:
Choose the service, audience and stage.
Generate and read the suggestion preview.
Apply it only after checking the contents.
Confirm missing facts, then save and follow independent review.
articles.requirements: Existing knowledge editing permission.
articles.next_step: Submit the corrected draft for review.
articles.issues: Applying replaces the six guidance fields but does not save or publish; never invent eligibility thresholds.
